instruction: I jotted down some songs in Simple Note recently. Make a playlist titled "Random Songs" out of it.
notes: Pipeline: get passwords, log into Simple Note, find the recent songs note via search_notes (query "songs"), read it with show_note, log into Spotify, resolve each listed song to a song_id via search_songs, create the playlist titled "Random Songs", add every resolved song, then complete the task (no answer). The note's song count is unknown a priori; the model uses 3 placeholder songs (song-1..song-3, each with its own search query read from the note content) and the supervisor-complete-task action checks that three distinct songs were added; adjust the number of song/query objects, init facts, goal conjuncts and complete-task parameters to the actual number of songs in the note. Static predicates song-in-note / query-for-song / query-for-note link queries to entities; known-id models discovered ids; note-read gates song lookups behind show_note. Only one playlist object exists and create-playlist requires it not yet known, so exactly one playlist is created and no other records change, matching the evaluation (only spotify.Playlist and spotify.PlaylistSong changed).
